items.evidence: versions/26.2/tools/test_model_baking_parity.py:client_libraries() (lines 58-68) builds the client classpath from the manifest only and does not append tools/jsr305-3.0.2.jar. The 1.21.7 Batch 0 fix for the identical defect (d7a14e91) is NOT in the 26.2 tree. Without jsr305, javac crashes (rc=4, CompletionFailure: class file for javax.annotation.Nullable not found) when compiling an oracle that completes a Nullable-referencing symbol — a latent crash across the oracle_harness drivers. The measurement adds jsr305 itself, so the numbers above are unaffected. Fix direction: append jsr305 in client_libraries() — one point, fixes all users. Not fixed in this batch (measurement + triage only).

items.evidence: No driver was run in this batch (measurement + triage only), so the runtime-failure layer the 1.21.7 sample found (a compiling oracle throwing NullPointerException at runtime — Unsafe-allocated ClientLevel subclass) is unmeasured for 26.2. The 248 'runnable' drivers are runnable by javac only. Every repaired oracle needs an end-to-end driver run to confirm it yields a measurement; driver runs cost ~10-30 min each on this VM for the large harnesses, and client_probe builds OOM single-threaded under multi-agent load — a CI-or-quiet-window job, not a sweep-batch job.

systemic_note: Same root cause as the pilot's G1/G3/G5/G6, one version closer: the 26.2 tree carries 26.3 API forms (packages, constructors, abstract methods) for things that do not exist in vanilla 26.2, and every such reference fails loudly at javac time in the oracles (unlike the port code, where the same pattern silently degrades). Two mechanical groups (LocalPlayer ctor, 17 files; Level.fuelValues(), 4 files) rescue 21 files with two signature translations. The densityfunction (O4) and renderpearl/material.rule (O5) groups are the genuinely hard ones: 26.3-only APIs with no 26.2 equivalent to translate to import-by-import. Compiling is not running (O8) — the runtime layer is unmeasured and each oracle needs an end-to-end driver run.
